newsitem.title: USA: Senior members of Congress cast last votes.
newsitem.headline: Senior members of Congress cast last votes.

text.p: The adjournment of Congress for the year on Friday marks the end of the House and Senate careers of at least 56 members, including some of the best known lawmakers of both chambers.
Although their terms continue until next Jan. 3, no more votes are scheduled for the 42 representatives and 14 senators who will not be running for election on Nov. 5.
Another 10 House members are running for Senate seats, but only about half are favored. Several other House and Senate incumbents may be defeated in the voting.

Among the senior senators retiring are Rhode Island Democrat Claiborne Pell, who has served for 36 years, Oregon Republican Mark Hatfield, who was elected in 1966, and Democrats Sam Nunn of Georgia and Bennett Johnston of Louisiana, who are leaving after 24 years.

Other Senate retirees are Democrats James Exon of Nebraska, Howell Helfin of Alabama, David Pryor of Arkansas, Bill Bradley of New Jersey and Paul Simon of Illinois and Republicans Nancy Kassebaum of Kansas, William Cohen of Maine, Alan Simpson of Wyoming and Hank Brown of Colorado.
Brown is leaving after six years, Simon after 12 years and the other seven each served 18 years.

Republican Sheila Frahm of Kansas, who was appointed in June to replace Majority Leader Bob Dole after he quit to concentrate on his presidential campaign, was defeated in her bid for the nomination to run for the rest of Dole's term by Rep. Sam Brownback.
Most of the retirees said they wanted to spend more time with their families or pursue other careers.

"As a small forward with the New York Knicks and as U.S. senator from New Jersey, I believe I have had two of the best jobs in the world," said Bradley, 53, who was a professional basketball star before his election in 1978. "I am leaving the Senate, but I am not leaving public life," he added.
Cohen, 56, who also served six years in the House, said, "There is never a good time to leave the best job in the world. But for me, it is the best time."

Retiring House members include Democrat Sam Gibbons of Florida and Tennessee Republican James Quillen, who have each served 34 years, 30-year Democratic veterans Sonny Montgomery of Mississippi, Andy Jacobs of Indiana and Tom Bevill of Alabama and Colorado Democrat Patricia Schroeder, the senior women in Congress after 24 years.

Two first-term House Republicans, Enid Greene of Utah and Wes Cooley of Oregon, are also quitting. Greene is leaving because of an investigation of her former husband and campaign finance chairman Joseph Waldholdz and Cooley is not running because of charges that he lied about his military record.
